report.summary: Section 6 makes multiple unsupported claims about novelty and feasibility of latent cross-plane discovery without citing any prior art or addressing known failures of similar approaches.
risks: 6.1 | high | Claim of 'schema-light Node Cards' with a fixed set of fields contradicts 'schema-light' and is not novel; similar constructs exist in knowledge graphs (e.g., RDF quads, 2004). | Compare with existing knowledge graph node models that include identity, revision, provenance, etc.

6.2 | medium | 'never receives a literally schema-free graph' is vague and self-contradictory given 'schema-light'; the minimum contract is not justified. | Check if the stated minimum fields are indeed necessary and sufficient for cross-plane discovery.

6.3 | high | Claim that latent layer 'proposes typed cross-plane bindings with score and rationale' is a restatement of standard embedding-based link prediction; no novelty. | Survey embedding-based link prediction methods (e.g., TransE, 2013; RotatE, 2019) that already produce typed relations with scores.

6.4 | high | 'A verifier checks source evidence, revision compatibility, ...' is a generic pipeline also used in knowledge base construction (e.g., Google Knowledge Vault, 2014). | Compare with existing verification pipelines in knowledge base construction.

6.5 | medium | 'Unverified similarities remain proposals and expire or are retested' is vague and lacks mechanism; similar to temporal decay in recommendation systems. | Check if any existing system implements this expiry mechanism and how it performs.

6.6 | low | '4fold Project-Twin IR + latent cross-plane discovery + evidence-bound promotion' is an unsupported formula; unclear how it is 'canonical'. | No prior art needed, but the claim is unfalsifiable without definition.

6.7 | low | 'Forest is the teacher; the latent atlas is the hypothesis machine; the evaluator is the truth boundary' is metaphorical and not a technical claim. | Not falsifiable; no observation can settle it.
todos: Replace 'schema-light' with a precise definition of the node card schema and justify its minimality.
Cite existing work on embedding-based link prediction and verification pipelines to acknowledge prior art.
Clarify the 'expire or retest' mechanism with specific design or reference to known systems.
Define the 'canonical formula' with concrete architecture or remove the claim.

claims.claim: Embeddings may consume schema-light Node Cards with stable node identity, revision, plane, source locator, compact content, local neighborhood, and provenance.
claims.why: The claim is not novel; knowledge graphs already use similar node representations (e.g., RDF quads with graph identifiers, 2004). The term 'schema-light' is misleading because the listed fields constitute a fixed schema. Prior art: RDF 1.1 (2014), Wikidata (2012) uses entity identifiers, revision, etc.

claims.claim: A shared embedding space can retrieve possible relations without a single giant ontology, but it never receives a literally schema-free graph: identity, revision, plane, provenance, and relation-candidate shape are the minimum contract.
claims.why: The claim is self-contradictory: 'schema-light' vs. 'minimum contract'. It is also unclear what 'relation-candidate shape' means. No evidence that this minimum contract is necessary or sufficient. Prior art: embedding spaces in knowledge graphs (e.g., TransE, 2013) do not require such a contract.

claims.claim: The latent layer is a hypothesis machine. It proposes typed cross-plane bindings with score and rationale.
claims.why: This is exactly what embedding-based link prediction does (e.g., TransE, 2013; RotatE, 2019). The addition of 'rationale' is vague and not novel; some methods provide explanations (e.g., knowledge graph attention networks, 2019).

claims.claim: A verifier checks source evidence, revision compatibility, type/rule constraints, and task relevance before an edge becomes trusted.
claims.why: This is a standard verification pipeline in knowledge base construction (e.g., Google Knowledge Vault, 2014; DeepDive, 2015). The claim does not specify how these checks are implemented or what makes them novel.

claims.claim: Unverified similarities remain proposals and expire or are retested.
claims.why: This is a common mechanism in systems with temporal decay (e.g., recommendation systems, knowledge graph completion with time, e.g., TComplEx, 2020). No specific mechanism or novelty is claimed.

claims.claim: Canonical formula: 4fold Project-Twin IR + latent cross-plane discovery + evidence-bound promotion
claims.why: The formula is not defined; '4fold Project-Twin IR' is unexplained. No claim that can be tested. It is a slogan, not a technical statement.

claims.claim: Forest is the teacher; the latent atlas is the hypothesis machine; the evaluator is the truth boundary.
claims.why: This is metaphorical language with no operational meaning. It cannot be verified or refuted.
